questions.heading: The Builder's Scans Grew Faster Than the Fleet, but the Solve Is What Takes the Time
questions.stem: On some machine a 5,000-unit run takes about 19 seconds. A teammate proposes rebuilding the model as a proto from arrays. What does the lesson's measurement suggest?

options.text: It buys little, since the solve takes most of the run
options.says: Right: the solve was 95% of the run; the build under a second.

options.text: It is needed, since the build takes most of the run
options.says: The build took 0.80 s of a run whose solve took 17.66 s.

options.text: It is needed, since the model grows faster than the fleet
options.says: Variables, rows and nonzeros grow about tenfold for a tenfold fleet.

options.text: It is needed, since the coefficients are the slow part

questions.heading: The Tests Hold the Fast Code to the Slow Code
questions.stem: Why do the scale tests not include a test that the fast builder is at least twice as fast as the reference?

options.text: Timing tests are slow, since a 5,000-unit build takes minutes
options.says: The fast build of 5,000 units took 0.65 s.

options.text: The fast builder is not faster, so such a test would fail
options.says: It was faster at every size measured.

options.text: A busy machine could fail it, so tests check the model, not time
options.says: Right: the tests check what the speed-up must not change.

options.text: The reference builder is gone, so there is nothing to time
options.says: It is kept as `build_reference`, the definition of the model.

questions.heading: A Request Scales With Its Fleet, in One Place
questions.stem: Planners raise the pilot request's crew-weeks from 12 to 14 and run the 5,000-unit plan with `Request.scaled(10)`. What happens to that plan's request?

options.text: Nothing, since the 5,000-unit request is written by hand
options.says: It is derived from the pilot's with `scaled`, not written separately.

options.text: Its crew-weeks become 140, since it is derived from the pilot's
options.says: Right: one place holds the limits, and `scaled` multiplies them.

options.text: Its crew-weeks stay at 120, since scaled leaves crews alone
options.says: `scaled` multiplies the crew-weeks with the other limits.

options.text: Its outage cost rises tenfold, since every field is scaled
options.says: The outage cost, years, window and rate are not scaled.
